No topic has two or more graded reviews yet, so there is no spread in response time to measure.

Volatility is the coefficient of variation (SD ÷ mean) of your response times per topic. Higher is better — it means your timing varies, which is what thinking looks like. The %1$s line is an interpretation of an unitless threshold in the brainlift, not a fitted constant.
(%1$d topic(s) not shown: fewer than two graded reviews, so volatility is undefined rather than zero.)

✗ Rote pattern detected — %1$d%% of measurable topics show near-identical response times (volatility below %2$s); at most %3$d%% is allowed.
This is not a data-volume problem. Reviews that all take the same time look like recognising the card rather than retrieving the fact, so a score computed from them would not mean what it appears to mean.
✗ Refusing to score — the backend did not say which rule failed. That is a bug worth reporting, not a judgement about your studying.
